full_judgment: 9. The appellants have filed the certified copies of S.A. Khatian Nos. 154 and 190 in this Court by way of additional evidence and after hearing the learned Advocates of both the parties we have accepted the certified copies of S.A. Khatians Nos. 154 and 190 as additional evidence on the ground that the Khatians are public documents. The learned Advocate for plaintiff respondent No.1 has submitted that the plaintiff having claimed the entire .12 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No. 77 of plot No. 699 and he having not claimed the rest .35 decimals of land of plot No. 699 recorded in S.A. Khatians Nos. 154 and 190, the suit does not suffer from defect of party and in support of his submission he has relied upon the case of Mir Shariatullah Vs. Abdur Rahman Bapary and others, 8 DLR (DA) 645. In the case reported in 7 P.L.R. (DA) 619 it has been held that the suit for partition is incompetent if all the co- owners are not parties to the suit as no effective decree can be passed in the absence of anyone of them. In the case reported in 10. P.L.R. (DA) 27 it has been held that the suit for partition without bringing the rest of the land of the tenancy into the hotchpotch and without impleading the other parties interested in the land, is not maintainable. In the case reported in 26 DLR (H.C.) 363 arising out of a suit for recovery of possession on declaration of title it has been held that it is one of the established principles of judicial procedure that no Court shall pass a decree which is infructuous and can be set at naught at the will of a person who has not been made a party to the suit. In the case reported in 31 DLR (AD) 218 it has been observed :- "All objections on the ground of non-Joinder or misjoinder of parties’ ought to have been taken at the earliest possible opportunity and any such objection not so taken be deemed to have been waived. Having regard to the law of procedure, it can pertinently be contended that the defendants cannot raise the question of non-joinder of parties for the first time in the court of first appeal. No Court should pass an infructuous decree. If it comes to the notice of the Court that for the absence of a party who was a necessary party in the suit, the decree which may be passed may run into jeopardy, the Court may not pass such a decree."
